key_insight: A graph neural network can learn cross-functional energy corrections, aligning heterogeneous DFT formation energies onto a common high-accuracy scale.
engineering_relevance: This enables legacy PBE datasets to be upgraded toward r2SCAN-like quality, improving materials screening for phase stability, batteries, and reaction thermodynamics.
method: Train on 380,190 structurally paired PBE-r2SCAN entries from MatPES
Predict residual energy offsets from atomic structure with a GPTFF-based GNN
Apply learned corrections to convert PBE energies to r2SCAN-level estimates
evidence_signal: On the MatPES benchmark, the model achieved 14.3 meV/atom MAE for PBE-to-r2SCAN conversion, outperforming CHGNet at 18.2 meV/atom.
watch_item: Performance depends on the availability and representativeness of paired cross-functional training data, so transfer to new chemistries or DFT settings may require recalibration.
paper_title: Aligning Heterogeneous DFT Datasets: A Graph Neural Network Approach to Cross-Functional Formation Energies
